learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Ability to manage information, handle and apply technical specifications and necessary legislation for engineering practice.
Adequate knowledge of the concept of a company, its institutional and legal framework. Organization and management of companies.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK I: COMPANY, ENTREPRENEUR AND DECISIONS IN THE COMPANY
TEMA 1. The company and the entrepreneur.
The company as a conceptual reality.
BLOCK II: FUNCTIONAL AREAS OF THE COMPANY
TEMA 2. Organization of the company's productive activity.
The production function: production of goods and production of services.
The goals of the production function.
Strategic and tactical decisions in productive activity.
Nature and scope of the financial function.
The economic-financial cycles and structure of the company.
Concept, content and functions of marketing in the company.
The control function: types of control.
BLOCK IV: THE STRATEGIC APPROACH OF THE COMPANY
teaching_methods: Exposition of theory and general examples
Active learning methods (just in time teaching, team based learning, cooperative learning, cases, project-based learning)

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities
Delivery of exercises and/or practical cases
Active learning in face-to-face classes (formative and summative assessment)

assessment_rules: The grading system is governed by RD 1125/2003. Students can choose between two evaluation options. Option A (without continuous assessment) consists of a final written theoretical-practical exam (60% theory, 30% practical) plus 10% for attendance to practical classes and submission of at least two required activities. Option B (with continuous assessment) consists of 30% from active learning in class, 30% from the theoretical exam, 30% from the practical exam, and 10% from activities in practical sessions. All students, regardless of the chosen option, must obtain a minimum score of 4 out of 10 in both the theoretical and practical parts of the final exam to pass the subject.
